subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server TCP and Unix WebSocket handshakes both fail after a fixed 30-second deadline?
rationale: Source and proof establish that an unbounded wait is defective, but repository evidence does not define the acceptable maximum handshake latency for slow remote or tunneled Codex deployments.

options.title: Approve 30 seconds
options.body: Accept the shared 30-second deadline because it bounds indefinite hangs and aligns with existing gateway handshake floors.

options.title: Choose another deadline
options.body: Set a different documented constant and update the regression and real-behavior proof expectations accordingly.

options.title: Require transport-specific deadlines
options.body: Keep separate TCP and Unix deadlines if maintainers expect materially different latency or trust characteristics.

recommendation.title: Approve 30 seconds
recommendation.body: Accept the shared 30-second deadline because it bounds indefinite hangs and aligns with existing gateway handshake floors.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Codex app-server transport and lifecycle work provides the strongest available ownership signal for this availability tradeoff.
